item.title: EFCC uncovers illegal Chinese-run oil refinery in Ogun
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has uncovered an illegal refinery in Ogere, Ogun State, where Chinese nationals allegedly processed sludge oil into diesel for sale in the Nigerian market. The discovery followed a raid by operatives of the commission’s Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 on Saturday, October 31, after intelligence and surveillance linked the facility to suspected illegal sludge oil refining. The EFCC, in a statement by its Head of Media and Publicity, Dele Oyewale, on Tuesday, said the facility was deserted when operatives stormed the premises, following an earlier clampdown on four illegal lithium processing plants in the area. But the operatives found waste products from the refining process, underground tanks believed to have been used for heating and processing sludge oil, and substances suspected to be diesel. “However, waste products from the refining process were discovered at the location,” the commission said. Two of the underground tanks inspected contained substances suspected to be Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), commonly known as diesel. Preliminary investigations showed that the operators sourced sludge oil, also known as black sludge, from Warri, Delta State, and Port Harcourt, Rivers State, before transporting it to the facility in Ogere for processing. According to the EFCC, the suspected operators subjected the sludge oil to intense heat, allowing lighter petroleum components to pass through a series of chambers and filters in a process believed to produce diesel for sale in the Nigerian market. The commission said security personnel at the facility told its operatives that the Chinese operators never disclosed their identities or the name of the company behind the operation. “Security personnel at the facility told EFCC operatives that the Chinese operators never disclosed their identities nor the name of the company behind the facility,” the statement said. The EFCC said it had taken over the premises as investigations continued to establish the identities of the operators, the ownership of the facility and the full extent of the suspected illegal activities. It added that the investigation would also determine the extent of the suspected economic sabotage linked to the operation. “Consequently, operatives of the Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 of the EFCC have since taken over the premises as investigations continue to establish the identities of the operators, the ownership of the facility and the full extent of the suspected illegal activities and economic sabotage,” the commission said. item.title: Reps invite CBN governor over alleged unpaid pensions
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives on Tuesday resolved to invite the Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, Olayemi Cardoso, to explain alleged breaches of pension agreements and the non-payment of benefits to retired employees of the apex bank. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion on Tuesday titled, “Need to investigate the Central Bank of Nigeria for alleged breach of approved pension agreements, non-implementation of harmonisation policy and exclusion of pensioners from general pension increases.” The motion was moved by the member representing Igabi Federal Constituency of Kaduna State, Hussaini Jallo. Presenting the motion, Jallo expressed concern over alleged non-compliance with contractual agreements governing the pension entitlements and welfare of retired CBN employees. He said the alleged non-implementation and faulty execution of the harmonisation policy might have resulted in disparities in pension benefits and the accumulation of unpaid arrears, leaving affected pensioners in financial hardship. “The House is concerned that the alleged non-implementation and faulty execution of the harmonisation policy may have led to disparities in pension benefits and the accumulation of unpaid arrears, ultimately denying rightful entitlements and imposing severe financial hardship on affected pensioners who depend on these funds for their livelihood,” he said. The lawmaker also raised concerns over allegations that some pensioners had been excluded from general pension increases on the grounds of additional or extra-statutory demands that might not be consistent with applicable laws, binding agreements or approved pension policies. Jallo further disclosed that the number of CBN pensioners had declined from 5,104 in 2011 to approximately 3,000, representing a reduction of more than 2,100. He said the figures translated to an average loss of 140 pensioners annually, adding that the mortality rate was likely to increase as the surviving retirees advanced in age. The lawmaker warned that prolonged delays in pension payments could expose elderly and vulnerable retirees to poverty, ill health and avoidable loss of life. He argued that retirees who had served the country deserved fairness, transparency and the prompt payment of all benefits lawfully due to them. “The House acknowledges the need for legislative oversight to establish the facts, determine the extent of any breaches or administrative failures, and ensure that all eligible pensioners receive their lawful entitlements,” he said. The motion received overwhelming support from lawmakers when it was subjected to a voice vote during plenary presided over by Speaker Tajudeen Abbas. item.title: 24-yr-old runner dies after collapsing two miles from NYC Marathon finish line
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A 24-year-old first-time New York City Marathon runner, Rachel Apa, has died after collapsing just two miles from the finish line during the race in Central Park, with her father revealing that she suffered from a rare condition known as rhabdomyolysis. Apa collapsed at about 1:30 p.m. on Sunday, November 1, while competing in the 26.2-mile race. She was rushed to Mount Sinai Hospital, where she died at 9:40 p.m., according to her father, Steve Apa. Her father told The New York Times that she died from rhabdomyolysis, a condition that causes damaged muscle tissue to break down and release substances into the bloodstream, potentially damaging vital organs, including the kidneys. He expressed shock over her death, describing his daughter as being in excellent health and physical condition before the race. “It’s unfathomable,” he said, adding that she was in “perfect health, perfect shape, 24 years old.” Apa, a graduate of Bucknell University and former college field hockey player, had spent months preparing for her first marathon. During her collapse, a hospital social worker, Michaela Nicholas, reportedly rushed to help but could not find a pulse. Two doctors watching the race also took turns performing cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) before medical personnel arrived with a defibrillator. Apa was running as part of the Parkinson’s Foundation Champions programme to raise awareness and funds in memory of her grandfather, who died from Parkinson’s disease in 2022. On her fundraising page, she described him as her childhood role model, saying he taught her to stay active, push her limits and embrace challenges. She also explained that watching the disease gradually take away his ability to move had made the cause particularly meaningful to her. New York Road Runners, the organisation responsible for the marathon, expressed sadness over her death and extended its condolences to her family, friends and the running community. “We are deeply saddened by the death of one of our runners following yesterday’s race. Our thoughts and sincere sympathies are with the runner’s family, friends, and the entire running community,” the organisation said. Rhabdomyolysis, sometimes called rhabdo, occurs when muscle tissue breaks down and releases proteins and other substances into the bloodstream. Severe cases can cause kidney damage, kidney failure and other life-threatening complications. Although it can affect anyone, intense physical exertion can trigger the condition. item.title: Trump cites immigration, Iran, tariffs in election day pitch
item.description: US President Donald Trump defended his record Tuesday in a final TV phone-in pitch to voters on the morning of midterm elections, saying he had rebuilt the country through his immigration crackdown, war on Iran and tariff policy. “We have to keep America great. We’re great now. We were terrible two years ago,” Trump told the “Fox & Friends” show as Americans voted in elections that could see his Republican Party lose control of Congress. Polls predict Democrats will win the House of Representatives and have a shot at the Senate, and Trump, whose own ratings have plunged, targeted his last-minute message at his right-wing base. “We were a laughing stock all over the world,” he said. “The leaders of other countries didn’t even take us seriously. They thought we were fools, and we’re hot now. We’re the hottest country in the world. We’re respected by everybody. “We’re going to keep it that way and get better.” In his second term, Trump has dramatically cut the number of migrants crossing the US border from Mexico and launched a war on Iran that has caused gas prices to soar for Americans. “When I took over, the border was open. We were having millions and millions of people pour in, many criminals and murderers,” he said, repeating his often baseless or exaggerated claims. “They were released from jails from the Congo in Africa, from all over South America, from Asia. They were pouring into our country. It was just a horrible sight, and they were very dangerous.” “The inflation is solved,” he added, “And the Hormuz Strait, we have total control of it with the Navy blockade (on Iran). I mean, everything’s going good. “Car companies are pouring in because they don’t want to pay tariffs.” The post Trump cites immigration, Iran, tariffs in election day pitch appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Full list: 28 states that approved state police
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The National Assembly has confirmed that 28 State Houses of Assembly have approved the proposed establishment of state police in Nigeria, paving the way for the constitutional amendment bill to be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu for assent. According to the Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, the 28 approvals exceed the two-thirds majority required under Section 9 of the 1999 Constitution, which translates to 24 states. The National Assembly can therefore proceed with the next stage of the process towards presidential assent. Read Also: 28 states approve State Police Bill as NASS moves to transmit to Tinubu The bill was forwarded to the 36 state assemblies on September 16, 2026, for consideration, with October 15 initially set as the deadline for them to communicate their decisions. Ogunlana, however, said his office would continue to receive and verify reports from the assemblies ahead of the bill’s transmission to Tinubu. The 28 states that have approved the proposed establishment of state police are listed below: Adamawa Delta Edo Kwara Nasarawa Ogun Osun Oyo Plateau Rivers Taraba Zamfara Enugu Anambra Imo Ekiti Kebbi Akwa Ibom Bayelsa Benue Cross River Abia Yobe Kaduna Lagos Kano Sokoto Ebonyi The post Full list: 28 states that approved state police appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US-bound passengers must declare DR Congo travel history under new Ebola rules
item.description: US-bound air passengers must sign a statement that they have not travelled to the Democratic Republic of Congo, the epicentre of a deadly Ebola outbreak, under new rules coming into force on Tuesday, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Africa’s latest Ebola outbreak has killed more than 5,300 people, the vast majority of them in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), according to the continent’s top health agency. Anyone boarding an international flight to the United States must sign a statement that they have not been present in the DRC in the 21 days before their travel, according to the CDC. The CDC said the rules are required as “a public health measure intended to reduce the risk of Ebola being introduced into the United States through air travel.” The post US-bound passengers must declare DR Congo travel history under new Ebola rules appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Senate rejects move to revive Nigeria Airways, Air Nigeria
item.description: *** Urges FG to re-ajudge BASA agreement for Nigeria Air services fly directly to China *** Says we should not waste time on dead issues; calls for a national carrier with Nigeria’s flag *** We can’t revive what is already dead, Akpabio. By Henry Umoru, Abuja The Senate has rejected calls for the revival of Nigeria Airways and Air Nigeria while it urged the Federal Government to renegotiate and enforce Nigeria’s Bilateral Air Services agreement, BASA, with China to allow Nigerian airlines to operate direct flights to the Asian country. According to the Senate, there was the urgent need for a review of existing aviation arrangements to address the imbalance in flight operations between both countries and ensure that Nigerian carriers enjoy reciprocal access to China directly. The Upper Chamber has also urged the Federal Government to explore ways of establishing a viable national carrier that would fly the nation’s flag to ease the challenges confronting Nigerian air travellers rather than what it described as wasting time in discussing dead issues. The Senate also asked the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs to initiate diplomatic talks with China regarding business visa facilitation for Nigerian traders and reciprocal slot allocations to Chinese airports. Resolutions of the Senate on Tuesday were a sequel to a motion titled “Enforcing the Bilateral Air Service Agreement (BASA)”. The motion was moved by the Senate Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno, APC, Borno North. The Upper Chamber has mandated the committees on Aviation and Foreign Affairs to ensure compliance and report to the Senate in 4 weeks. The Senate also noted the growing trade relationship between both countries and the need for Nigeria to maximise the economic benefits of that partnership. An additional prayer by Senator Ned Nwoko, APC, Delta North, to revive the defunct airline sparked an additional debate as it was dismissed. The President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, said, “We can’t revive what is already dead.” Instead, the leadership advised pursuing an entirely new, viable national carrier. Senator Akpabio, who questioned the wisdom of reviving an airline that had long ceased operations, said, . ‘We can’t revive what is already dead. Did Nigerian airways ever work? While acknowledging the importance of having a Nigerian-owned airline, the President of the Senate recalled that the country once operated a fleet of nearly 40 aircraft and how Nigeria got to where we are, saying, “Common campaigns, we cannot have planes to hire.” Akpabio, however, warned that Nigeria might have to reconsider the privileges granted to Chinese airlines if Nigerian carriers were not allowed reciprocal access to operate direct flights to China. item.title: Waste crisis: LAWMA records improved truck turnaround at Olusosun dumpsite after upgrade
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos Waste Management Authority, LAWMA, has recorded improved truck turnaround and reduced compactor queues at the Olusosun dumpsite following the extension and stabilisation of its E1 tipping platform. LAWMA’s Executive Director, Finance, Mr Kunle Adebiyi, disclosed this on Tuesday, saying the upgrade has enhanced the efficiency of waste discharge operations and significantly reduced waiting time for compactors by facilitating faster evacuation of waste. According to him, “the improved turnaround has also strengthened LAWMA’s capacity to clear accumulated waste backlogs and address identified black spots across the state.” Adebiyi however, expressed concern over continued indiscriminate disposal of waste and re-emergence of refuse at locations previously cleared, warning that such practices undermine sanitation efforts. He urged residents to desist from dumping refuse on road medians and other unauthorised locations, particularly in areas recently cleared by the authority, and to patronise their assigned Private Sector Participation, PSP, operators for proper collection and disposal. Adebiyi reiterated that sustaining a cleaner Lagos requires collective responsibility, calling on residents to support ongoing efforts by adopting responsible disposal practices. He said LAWMA remains committed to strengthening operational efficiency and improving waste evacuation across the state for a cleaner and healthier Lagos. item.title: UEFA to observe one-minute silence for Tenerife forward who died at 30
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye UEFA will observe a one-minute silence at all its matches this week in honour of CD Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel Alameda, who has died at the age of 30. The European football governing body announced the tribute on Tuesday, November 3, following the death of the Spanish striker, which has drawn tributes from across European and Spanish football. In a statement shared on its official X account, UEFA said the football community was mourning the loss of De Miguel and extended its condolences to his family, friends and teammates. “We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends and teammates during this incredibly difficult time,” the statement read. UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin also expressed sadness over the forward’s death, saying the governing body had struggled to find words to describe the loss. “We are heartbroken by the death of Jesús de Miguel Alameda,” Čeferin said. “We have searched for words and found only silence. In that silence, our hearts and thoughts are with his family, his teammates, everyone at CD Tenerife, and all those who mourn this tragic loss.” De Miguel, who played for several clubs in Spain’s lower divisions, helped Tenerife secure promotion to the Segunda División last season. CD Tenerife confirmed his death in a statement, saying he passed away at 8:00 a.m. on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. The club described the news as devastating and said there were no words to ease the grief felt by his family, loved ones and the Tenerife football community. It also conveyed the family’s appreciation for the messages of support received, while appealing for their privacy to be respected during the difficult period. The Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) also paid tribute to the striker, expressing its condolences to his family, friends, CD Tenerife and the club’s supporters. The federation described his death as a loss to Spanish football. Vanguard News The post UEFA to observe one-minute silence for Tenerife forward who died at 30 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: High Court Hears Bid To Overturn Australia Social Media Ban
item.description: Australia’s landmark social media ban faces a legal test on Tuesday, as online platform Reddit urges the nation’s highest court to scrap the world-leading restrictions. Social media companies have been forced to purge millions of accounts after Australia banned under-16s from the likes of Facebook, TikTok and Reddit last December. The High Court of Australia will sit on Tuesday and Wednesday as Reddit, one of the most popular websites in the world, argues the laws are misguided and should be overturned. Reddit has highlighted a number of issues in its written submission to the court, pointing to problems enforcing the ban and a lack of scientific evidence about the harms of social media. “The evidence so far is that the effectiveness of the ban has been limited,” reads Reddit’s submission. Australia’s ban works by restricting children under 16 from holding accounts on the world’s biggest social media platforms. Map of Australia These platforms are responsible for weeding out underage users and face hefty fines if they are found to be falling short of their obligations. Reddit argued this approach was actually more dangerous, as registered accounts were governed by in-built safety features. Material posted on many online platforms and social media sites could still be accessed without an account, Reddit said. “Young people using other platforms without an account are also unable to be protected from exposure to particular harmful content as they previously had been,” its submission read. Australia said its restrictions would protect young users from graphic content, online predators and predatory algorithms designed to keep people scrolling. While there is a growing body of evidence about the harms of social media, Reddit argued there was no “scientific consensus”. Political discourse Reddit, which has also argued it should be exempt from the ban, said there was little research on whether certain platforms were safer than others. The High Court will also consider arguments from Australia’s Digital Freedom Project, which believes the ban restricts teens’ ability to take part in political discourse. “Social media is an important means of accessing news and engaging in political communication for young Australians, including children under 16,” the advocacy group argued in written submissions. “The restriction also risks removing beneficial sources of connection, support and participation,” it added. Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project separately announced last year they would challenge the ban. It was not clear how long it would take the high court to consider the case, although even the quickest decisions typically take months. Social media firms face mounting scrutiny over their use of allegedly addictive algorithms and stand accused of directing users to extreme content to keep them scrolling. item.title: Americans vote in midterms set to upend Trump presidency
item.description: Americans voted on Tuesday in pivotal midterm elections with Democrats hoping to seize control of Congress and impose the first significant checks on Donald Trump’s chaotic second term in the White House. Republicans losing the House would give Democrats the power to stall Trump’s legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration. A Senate defeat would also threaten his ability to appoint Supreme Court justices and senior officials. The election amounts to a nationwide judgment on Trump, with the mood turning sharply against Republicans amid anger over soaring living costs and the war against Iran. All 435 House seats and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are at stake, along with governorships in 36 states. Democrats need only three House gains and a net four seats in the Senate to wrest both chambers from Republican hands. Trump returned to office last year promising to bring down prices, but inflation, tariffs and fuel costs inflated by the Middle East conflict have squeezed Americans. The 80-year-old’s approval rating has hovered near the low 30s. In the suburbs of Atlanta, Georgia, retired teacher Jane Callum, 77, was among Democrats canvassing for Senator Jon Ossoff who framed the race as a watershed moment for the country’s future. “I really feel an obligation to do everything that I possibly can to change the direction that our country is going in now, and put it more on the path to democracy and away from autocracy,” she told AFP. Economic discontent Republicans insist that Trump’s tax cuts and immigration crackdown will benefit Americans, and they are portraying Democratic candidates as left-wing radicals. But in his final public campaign appearance on Monday, Trump barely touched on the economy and spent most of the time in a rambling talk about his problem-plagued renovation of Washington’s Reflecting Pool. “This is the last day before the midterm elections, the most important midterm I believe in our lifetime,” he said, 26 minutes into the speech, before quickly returning to talking about renovations. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer branded it a “pathetic closing message.” Some Republican supporters remain confident. “We’re going to win. As a matter of fact, we’ve probably already won,” Texas military veteran Yvonne Clouser told AFP. But while Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority, the political battlefield is extending into conservative states like Kansas, Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Alaska. Democrats must also defend competitive seats, including in Michigan, where a bitter internal dispute saw congresswoman Haley Stevens endorse Republican Mike Rogers rather than the Democratic nominee, Abdul El-Sayed. Decision Desk HQ’s final forecast projected 241 House seats for Democrats against 194 for Republicans, and a narrower 52-48 Democratic Senate majority. Disputed results? item.title: TikTok Dance: Feminist group slams Hisbah over arrest Of 3 women in Kano
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA-The Feminist Digital Watch (FemDigital Watch) has condemned the arrest and arraignment of popular TikTok creator Amani Ishaq and two others by the Kano State Hisbah Board over dance videos posted on social media. The collective, convened by the Redefining Alternative Civic Engagement for Africa (RACE Centre), said Hauwa Khamis and Sa’adatu Muhammad were arrested alongside Ishaq for allegedly contravening public morality and religious guidelines. They were arraigned before Magistrate Court No. 5, Court Road, Kano. This was contained in a statement signed by Evelyn Ugbe on behalf of the collective, in Abuja, on Tuesday. FemDigital Watch said while charges, bail conditions and detention status were still being verified, the incident marks a “troubling escalation in the systemic surveillance and criminalization of women’s creative self-expression in digital spaces.” According to the group, the targeting of the three women is not isolated enforcement of local ordinances but reflects an entrenched pattern of technology-facilitated, gender-based suppression. “Across Nigeria’s digital ecosystem, women creators consistently face disproportionate scrutiny, online mobbing, and state-backed censorship for routine digital expression that is widely normalized for men,” the statement said. The group said weaponization of morality laws to police women’s online participation shrinks civic and creative space for female creators who rely on platforms like TikTok for livelihood, encourages coordinated online abuse, and undermines constitutional rights. It said the action conflicts with Section 39 of the 1999 Constitution (as amended) which guarantees freedom of expression and Nigeria’s obligations under the Maputo Protocol. FemDigital Watch demanded immediate, unhindered access to legal representation and equitable bail terms for the three women and respect for their fundamental human rights without moral prejudice. It also called on the Kano State Hisbah Board and regulatory authorities to cease arbitrary surveillance, arrest and detention of female content creators exercising their right to peaceful freedom of expression and bodily autonomy online. The collective said it is documenting state-enforced and tech-facilitated abuses against women and girls and mobilizing legal-defense partners and civil society networks to track proceedings in Kano. item.title: Police investigate Spanish striker’s death after on-pitch collision with goalkeeper
item.description: Spain’s National Police have launched an investigation into the death of CD Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel following his collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono, with the case now under judicial supervision. Sources at the provincial police headquarters confirmed the development to AFP. De Miguel, 30, died at Nuestra Señora de La Candelaria Hospital, hours after sustaining serious injuries in a collision with Owono during Monday’s match at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López Stadium. “Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe this is real, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death, at 8:00 am (0700 GMT), of Jesus de Miguel Alameda,” his club Tenerife said in a statement. “No words can ease the pain, nothing can lessen this great feeling of sadness. Our thoughts are with the family, his close friends and Tenerife fans, who today are grieving over this terrible news.” The incident occurred in second-half stoppage time, with the score tied at 2-2, as the Tenerife striker chased an aerial ball beyond the halfway line. Spanish media said that De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest and was resuscitated. The player was taken to hospital and placed in intensive care, with Tenerife later saying that De Miguel’s condition had “worsened neurologically”, before his death. item.title: Osun APC backtracks, renames ‘parallel’ list as parliamentary campaign committee
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo Following protest from members and rejection of a parallel presidential campaign committee by the national leadership, the Osun State All Progressives Congress (APC) has renamed its earlier presidential/parliamentary campaign committee to just the parliamentary campaign committee. The Osun APC in statement signed by the Party Chairman on Monday had released a parallel presidential campaign committee list which has the Governorship candidate as its Director-General after the Presidential Campaign Council Coordinator, Governor Ademola Adeleke, had inaugurated a campaign committee in the state. However, three members of the State Executive Committee, Wole Adunola, State Publicity Secretary; Adesola Ayangbile, Welfare Officer; and Rasheed Adeniji, Asst. Organising Secretary, and Abiola Ololade, Ex-Officio, in a joint statement, rejected the list on the ground that it does not reflect due process and lacked inclusiveness. This reportedly led to the national leadership of the party rejecting the said campaign committee list. Meanwhile, the APC, in another statement issued by the party chairman, Tajudeen Lawal, on Tuesday, renamed the list as parliamentary campaign committee, retaining the party’s governorship candidate in the August 15 election as the Director-General. The statement attached to the list reads, “Following the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) by the national leader of our party and its presidential candidate, His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, on the 14th of October 2026 in Abuja, and the subsequent inauguration of the Osun State PCC by the Executive Governor of Osun State, His Excellency, Governor Ademola Nurudeen Jackson Adeleke, on the 22nd of October 2026, we consider it extremely important to therefore bolster the efforts of the PCC to deliver massive votes for the reelection of our President, His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu (GCFR) in the forthcoming general elections.” “We have therefore carefully selected out All Progressives Congress (APC) leaders and members in Osun State to actualise our collective desire of ensuring a round victory for the President as well as our National and State Assembly candidates. “As a party, we are resolute to work in unison with every member of the State Presidential Campaign to deliver on our mandate as we muster concerted efforts to ensure victory for all the National and State Assemblies candidates of our great party,” it added. item.title: Iran president says return to war benefits ‘no one’, after reported US strikes
item.description: Iran’s president Masoud Pezeshkian said on Tuesday that a return to war would benefit “no one”, hours after reported US strikes on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz. It came as US voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterm elections that threaten President Donald Trump’s grip on power. Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the US, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said the Islamic republic was “ready for battle with its finger on the trigger”, while deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Iran retained the right to “legitimate self-defence” after the strikes. But Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis “through dialogue”, adding that “no one will benefit from this war” if it reignited, and emphasising that the country’s supreme leader had recently granted the government new powers to negotiate issues previously “off-limits”. The US strikes, reported by The Wall Street Journal, CNN, The New York Times and other outlets, hit Qeshm island in the Hormuz waterway, a key flashpoint of the Middle East war that has upended global markets. Unnamed US officials cited by the outlets described the attacks as defensive in nature. The Journal said it was just the latest of several undeclared strikes. US Central Command did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment. – ‘Iran wants a settlement’ – The US and Israel launched their war with Iran with a massive wave of strikes in late February. The conflict has been stalemated for months. Asked if Israel was involved in the latest reported strikes, an Israeli military spokesperson told AFP, “No”. The reported Qeshm attack came just hours after Trump signalled a deal with Iran “could happen”, as US voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterms dominated by public dissatisfaction with the war and the inflation it has brought. “Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible,” Trump posted on his Truth Social platform. Iranian state news agency IRNA reported five explosions in rapid succession on Qeshm island, and that some residents reported seeing two aircraft flying in its skies. Ghalibaf said the ball was in Washington’s court. “The countries of the region should know that, just as the Islamic Republic of Iran stands ready for battle with its finger on the trigger, it has also given the American side a powerful and rational response,” he said in a televised speech. “The ball is now in America’s court to prevent war.” – ‘Committed’ – Qatar, a mediator in protracted indirect negotiations between the US and Iran, said it remained hopeful of an interim deal in the war. “Both parties remain committed to the negotiation process; as we mentioned, we are facilitating the real-time exchange of proposals between them,” foreign ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari told reporters. item.title: 28 states approve State Police Bill as NASS moves to transmit to Tinubu
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The National Assembly has received approval from 28 State Houses of Assembly for the proposed constitutional amendment seeking to establish state police in Nigeria. The approval exceeds the constitutionally required threshold of 24 states, representing two-thirds of the 36 State Houses of Assembly, paving the way for the transmission of the bill to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the reports received from the 28 state legislatures had been verified alongside their respective votes and proceedings. According to the statement, the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, which seeks to provide for the establishment of State Police Services and related matters, was transmitted to the 36 State Houses of Assembly on September 16, 2026, for consideration and approval. The state legislatures were initially given 30 days, ending October 15, to communicate their decisions to the National Assembly. However, Ogunlana said his office would continue to receive reports from the state assemblies until the bill is transmitted for presidential assent. He said, “Following the receipt and verification of the reports, the Office confirms that 28 State Houses of Assembly have approved the Bill. “This represents more than the constitutionally prescribed threshold of not less than two-thirds of the 36 State Houses of Assembly, equivalent to 24 States, as required under Section 9 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999.” The clerk explained that the National Assembly had undertaken administrative verification of the reports and accompanying votes and proceedings to establish their authenticity and ensure that they accurately reflected the decisions taken by the respective state legislatures. He also clarified that Section 9 of the Constitution does not expressly prescribe a third reading for a Constitution Alteration Bill, unlike the procedure applicable to ordinary bills. item.title: CDS seeks civilian support, intelligence sharing to tackle terrorism
item.description: The Chief of Defence Staff, Gen. Olufemi Oluyede, has called for the support of civilians and host communities in the fight against terrorism. Oluyede made the call while speaking to newsmen on the sidelines of the 2026 Chief of Naval Staff (CNS) annual retreat on Tuesday in Abuja. According to Oluyede, there is a need for jointness and synergy among all key security stakeholders. Oluyede, whose philosophy for security lays heavy emphasis on synergy, said that jointness goes beyond inter-agency cooperation and also includes the civilians and communities. “It is important for us to continue to emphasise jointness because no single service can do the job alone, it requires a collective effort.” He said the armed forces are collectively doing their very best to make Nigeria safer, adding that what they require from Nigerians are support, prayers and intelligence reports. “If you see anything, you should tell us because everything we’re doing relies on intelligence, and for that, we need community support,” he said. He said the support provided by Nigerians would aid push the country forward on all fronts. He assured Nigerians that things would continue to get better. item.title: Five players who died after on-field incidents
item.description: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died on Tuesday as a result of injuries he suffered in a sickening collision with FC Andorra’s goalkeeper in a Spanish second division match. The 30-year-old is sadly not a unique case of a player dying either on the pitch or because of an injury sustained during the match. AFP Sport highlights five such fatalities: Marc-Vivien Foe, June 2003 Cameroon midfielder Foe collapsed after a heart attack during a Confederations Cup semi-final against Colombia in Lyon, France. The former Manchester City, West Ham and Lyon player was carried from the pitch as medical staff tried to revive him with mouth-to-mouth resuscitation and oxygen. After trying to restart his heart for 45 minutes without success he was declared dead, aged just 28. His death prompted improvements in both the testing of footballers for heart problems and the treatment they can receive during matches, including training club medical teams in CPR and using defibrillators. Antonio Puerta, August 2007 Spain international Puerta, 22, collapsed while playing for Sevilla in a La Liga match against Getafe and died three days later from multiple organ failure stemming from prolonged cardiac arrest. It was three months after he had helped Sevilla to win the UEFA Cup. Spanish legend Sergio Ramos has a tattoo tribute to Puerta and wore a T-shirt dedicated to him as Spain won the 2010 World Cup. “Antonio has always been with me. The next game, I went out on the field with his shirt and for a long time after that, I wore one that was dedicated to him,” said Ramos. Phil O’Donnell, December 2007 The Motherwell captain died of heart failure towards the end of his side’s 5-3 Scottish Premier League win over Dundee United in December 2007. The 35-year-old midfielder collapsed just as he was about to be substituted and was treated for around five minutes on the field before being taken to a waiting ambulance. O’Donnell played for Scotland, Celtic and Sheffield Wednesday during his career and his death caused widespread grief in Scottish football, causing a number of fixtures to be postponed. “He was a man among boys in every sense, in his attitude, his professionalism and integrity and sincerity,” his manager Mark McGhee said. Cristiano Junior, August 2009 The 25-year-old Brazilian, who was then the highest paid footballer in India, collided with the opposing goalkeeper when he scored a goal for his club Dempo 12 minutes from time in the 2004 Federation Cup final in Bangalore. Junior, who had moved to India to earn enough money to build a house for his mother back home, collapsed and was immediately attended to by his Nigerian strike partner Santi Martins. Martins stayed with him until an ambulance whisked him off to hospital but he was pronounced dead on arrival having suffered cardiac arrest. “The match continued. item.title: Kogi varsity defends fee hike, cites NELFUND for 4,032 students
item.description: The vice-chancellor of Prince Abubakar Audu University (PAAU), Anyigba, Prof. Salisu Usman, says 4,032 students have been approved for loans under the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND). Usman said this while defending the university’s fee increase at an investigative hearing organised by the Kogi House of Assembly on Tuesday in Lokoja. The hearing followed a petition alleging arbitrary increases in fees by the managements of PAAU and Kogi State Polytechnic. The VC said the recent fee review was not arbitrary but part of a unified fee structure approved by the Kogi Government for its three state-owned universities. Usman said the review followed a government directive issued in 2024 to harmonise fees across state-owned tertiary institutions. He said that PAAU’s charges were comparatively lower than those of similar institutions in neighbouring states. According to him, much of the controversy centred on medical programmes such as Medicine and Surgery (MBBS), Nursing and Medical Laboratory Science, which require huge investments, particularly during clinical training. The VC commended his predecessor, Prof. Marietu Tenuche, for reintroducing the medical programmes, which collapsed in 2012. He also lauded former Gov. Yahaya Bello for supporting stranded medical students and commended Gov. Ahmed Ododo for sustaining medical education in the state. Usman said that 4,032 students had been approved for NELFUND loans totalling N536.7 million to pay school fees, while another 600 applications were pending. He urged students to take advantage of the scheme, which also provided a N20,000 monthly upkeep allowance, with repayment commencing two years after graduation upon securing gainful employment. Earlier, the Commissioner for Education, Mr Wemi Jones, said the government followed due process in reviewing fees, considering economic realities and the interests of parents and students. Jones said the directive was issued to PAAU in 2024 but implemented inconsistently across departments, prompting full implementation to ensure compliance. He dismissed claims that Kogi State Polytechnic increased its fees, saying its rector had instead reduced accommodation charges by N5,000. The Chairman, House Committee on Education, Mr Idris Maikudi, said the Assembly mandated relevant committees to investigate the petition and compare the institutions’ charges with those of neighbouring states. Mr Bode Ogunmola, representing Ogori-Magongo, called for sustained government support for medical education, lamenting that the only general hospital in his constituency had operated for years without a doctor due to personnel shortages. Mr Jibril Abu, representing Ajaokuta Constituency, expressed concern over the absence of the petitioners at the hearing. He commended President Bola Tinubu for introducing NELFUND to expand access to higher education.
